item.title: Future Beat Alliance - Hidden Emotion (30th Anniversary Edition) (3x12inch) - FBAHE30
item.description: Future Beat Alliance - Hidden Emotion (30th Anniversary Edition) (3x12inch) - FBAHE30
item.content:encoded: Originally released in 1997, Hidden Emotion was intended to be the debut album from Matthew Puffett's Future Beat Alliance project on Void Records. Due to complications with the distributor, it was never officially released. Only 50 white label copies were made, leaving the album as a long-lost underground release that gradually developed a cult following. Born from Puffett's early experiments with electronic equipment and the musical influences he absorbed throughout the 1980s and early 1990s, Hidden Emotion captures the raw, hardware-driven character of his early productions, combining melancholic melodies with atmospheric, distinctly Detroit influenced soundscapes. The anniversary edition brings together the original nine-track album, fully remastered, with four additional tracks: a brand-new remix of "Routine" by Tom Churchill.
item.dc:creator: Future Beat Alliance

item.title: Sebastian Mullaert - When The Night Kissed We Winnowed Away (12inch) - WP1
item.description: Sebastian Mullaert - When The Night Kissed We Winnowed Away (12inch) - WP1
item.content:encoded:
Wa Wu We Patterns is a new label from Sebastian Mullaert, dedicated to his ever-evolving explorations of improvisation and spontaneity. The initial releases will explore faster tempos and the more energetic territories of house and techno.
At the heart of each release are two different live interpretations of the same musical seeds, exploring how rhythm, melody and energy can shift, transform and take on different shapes.
The music is created through Sebastian's four-step process, which is based on the idea of allowing a musical forest to come to life, a forest that becomes a deep and wide expression of the artist. Each track represents one temporary possibility, one expression within the ongoing exploration of that forest.
The label also brings together two of Sebastian's passions: music and nature photography. Through his lens, the patterns and expressions of the natural world become an extension of his ongoing exploration of creativity. Each release features one of his photographs as the cover artwork, accompanied by a separate four-colour printed poster.
The first release, When the Night Kissed We Winnowed Away, explores two contrasting expressions of the dance floor. The A-side moves into darker, edgier territory, where melodic tension meets driving rhythms. On the B-side, the same musical idea unfolds into something gentler and warmer, with a softer melodic expression.
Two expressions, one origin. An invitation to explore the possibilities of improvisation.
Available on coloured vinyl, classic black vinyl, and digitally on all major platforms.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Mullaert

item.title: Vril - Miami Mall Incident (incl. Rene Wise Remix) (12inch) - T3R030
item.description: Vril - Miami Mall Incident (incl. Rene Wise Remix) (12inch) - T3R030
item.content:encoded: .Vril has developed a distinctive language within techno, shaped by atmospheric depth, textured chords and a strong sense of movement. On Miami Mall Incident, he explores a more direct, dancefloor-focused side of his sound, alongside a remix by Rene Wise and a rework of an earlier composition. Miami Mall Incident opens the record with a rough, uncompromising energy. Raw drums and dark, textured chords establish a dense, driving atmosphere. The familiar harmonic character of .Vril’s productions is present throughout, pushed into a more forceful and immediate direction. On In Via, Rene Wise offers a contemporary interpretation built around hypnotic repetition and dub-inflected atmosphere. Subtle rhythmic disruptions and carefully placed details give the track a restless quality beneath its steady momentum. The sound opens up into a slightly brighter space, with layers that gradually shift and develop around the groove. Torus Inversion Grid moves into warmer, more inviting territory, combining expansive dub chords with a steady, energetic pulse. Closing the record, Torus XXXII (.VRIL's 2026 Rework) revisits a track originally released on Giegling in 2014. Its memorable melody and atmospheric character remain intact, now carried by a driving beat that transforms the once beatless composition into a powerful dancefloor moment. Across four tracks, Miami Mall Incident captures different dimensions of .Vril’s sound, from raw, driving techno to atmospheric dub and melodic reinterpretation. The record also traces a connection between different periods of his work, with the closing rework offering a particularly compelling perspective on how an existing musical idea can evolve over time.
item.dc:creator: Vril

item.description: Matti Turunen - Rantaluhta EP (12inch) - SAVY007
item.content:encoded: Savy Records' seventh release marks the label debut of Matti Turunen, one half of Finnish electro outfit Morphology and a cult figure across the wider electro scene. Rantaluhta EP is a timeless masterpiece. Synth-heavy throughout, it moves from bass-driven, Detroit-rooted machinery into a more euphoric, rave-leaning close -- a record that shows real range within the electro spectrum. On the flip, veteran producer Carl Finlow, contributes a remix under his Silicon Scally alias, pushing 'Oleanterinkiitaja' into trippy and galactic machine-funk territory.

item.title: Cromby - Jackin Shit (12inch) - POTENCY011
item.description: Cromby - Jackin Shit (12inch) - POTENCY011
item.content:encoded:
''Potency continues apace with 'Jackin Shit', a gleefully self-explanatory EP from label founder Cromby. Following widely-played recent releases from Malik Kassim aka Retromigration, Trax Unit and Rhythms of Prescott, the prolific DJ and producer reaffirms his imprint's fundamentals with four upfront, high-energy tracks, each reflecting a different facet of the Belfast-via-Berlin producer's decades-deep understanding of house and techno history.
Title track 'Jackin' Shit' gets things moving with a rich blend of rolling basslines, liquid keys and diva'ed up vocal snippets. Lucid and groovy in the style of seminal East Coast vocal pleasures, Cromby's vision of house is nonetheless driven by a dusty kick drum that references Head High/WK7, or Paul Woolford in a warehouse somewhere... In contrast, 'Sense Control' places percussion front and centre, locking in a tight rhythm in order to ride out a liquid collage of acid lines, ecstatic piano and other blissfully wavy elements.
'Con Gas' establishes a tougher direction on the flip, finding Cromby's busier instincts reduced the simplest of ingredients - sub, bass and stabs - taking dancers deep into the bowels of house, replete with classic vocal call-outs, and yes, even a well-earned inbuilt spinback. Having exhibited such restraint, we're unceremoniously booted out of the cubicle and back toward the strobes for 'Cheeky Bump', a rubbery, driving dancefloor tool guaranteed to delay any impending cab home.
Colourful, charismatic and exclusively engineered for true party people, 'Jackin' Shit' finds Cromby returning to home turf on definitive form.''
item.dc:creator: Cromby

item.title: Hodge - Magenta Glow EP (EP) - IT056
item.description: Hodge - Magenta Glow EP (EP) - IT056
item.content:encoded: IT is celebrating the Detroit - Bristol connection with the ''Magenta Glow EP'' from Hodge. This began with Hodge playing for IT in Detroit, first at Return to the Source, and then at a spring party at Tangent, where he was so inspired by what he saw that he began composing music for these environments. It quickly expanded to a number of songs, each to be carefully mixed from their stems by BMG in the Interdimensional Laboratory on hardware to give the record the largest and most solid sonic footprint it could have, using the same process as the recent Andy Toth record and Alchemical Sisters album. Each song is unique, yet each is so strong it could be its own single. Science fiction themes are highlighted with ''Magenta Glow'' referencing Philip K. Dick, and ''Oankali'' being named after entities from Lilith's Brood by Octavia E. Butler.
item.dc:creator: Hodge

item.title: Benjamin Damage - UFO Incision (12inch) - T3R029
item.description: Benjamin Damage - UFO Incision (12inch) - T3R029
item.content:encoded: Benjamin Damage has long operated at the intersection of physical intensity and emotional depth, developing a distinct approach to Techno where machine-driven rhythms leave space for melody, atmosphere and movement. On UFO Incision, he pushes that balance across four tracks that move from expansive and melodic to increasingly stripped-back and rhythmically focused territory. Feel 4U opens with a rolling, tightly controlled groove. Dry, repetitive drums provide the drive, contrasted by bright, open pads that give the track a striking sense of space. Carefully placed vocal fragments cut through the arrangement, adding another layer of tension to a track that feels hard and propulsive while carrying a subtle melancholic depth. Solex expands the melodic side of the record. A shifting arpeggio forms its centre, moving against darker melodic tones, elevated pads and a captivating chopped vocal. Constant modulation keeps the track in motion, while a loose hi-hat groove offsets the rigidity of the low-end. Rather than settling into repetition, the arrangement continuously rises, falls and reshapes itself. The title track marks a shift in focus. Darker and more reduced, UFO Incision strips back much of the melodic language of the A- side in favour of rhythm and detail. Dry drums form a tightly locked groove, while bleeps, glitches and finely placed sonic interventions create complexity around a minimal framework. Precise and functional, it finds depth in the smallest movements. Orbitings closes the record with a warped take on acid. Swinging drums and a dry, hypnotic groove meet futuristic acid tones and deep, modulating stabs, creating a track that feels both stripped and constantly in motion. Across UFO Incision, Benjamin Damage moves between two sides of the same language: melody and function, openness and reduction, emotional weight and physical drive. Even at its most direct, detail and modulation keep the music evolving. Four tracks built for the floor without sacrificing depth or character.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Damage

item.title: Architectural Featuring Blu Aloe - Mirror#1: Ultrawaves (12inch) - MIR001
item.description: Architectural Featuring Blu Aloe - Mirror#1: Ultrawaves (12inch) - MIR001
item.content:encoded:
MIRRORS was founded as a record label based on the idea that each release is a small window into an unknown reality, a fragment of a universe we cannot fully comprehend, where music becomes a way to observe what lies beyond our reach.
The first Mirror: ''Ultrawaves,'' two tracks featuring sounds by Architectural and vocal collaboration from Berlin-based experimental artist Blu Aloe, who captures the Mirrors universe with incredible precision and vocal personality across two extended tracks.
A first transmission from the other side of the mirror, situated on the frontier between house and deep techno. A starting point for a universe that will gradually reveal itself through sound.
item.dc:creator: Architectural Featuring Blu Aloe

item.title: CARISTA - Everything Is Better With You (12inch) - UI022
item.description: CARISTA - Everything Is Better With You (12inch) - UI022
item.content:encoded:
CARISTA makes her long-awaited return to her own United Identities with ''Everything Is Better With You''. It finds her dialling up the intimacy without losing an ounce of the funk. A warm, acid-flecked house record about the places and people that can make anywhere feel like home, served with enough heartiness and punch that's perfect for club season.
The record stems from a deep-seated urge to craft something entirely personal; the vocal is CARISTA's own, a result of a discarded Ableton sample that lacked the necessary soul. By recording it herself, she captures a raw, magnetic intimacy. This process, taking standard materials and transmuting them into something deeply individual, mirrors the very alchemy found on the most transcendent dance floors. Whether you find yourself in a sea of strangers or flanked by your closest kin, there is a singular moment where every element aligns. It is a feeling of stepping past your own physical limits to truly experience the best of times.
item.dc:creator: CARISTA

item.title: Foobar - Shifting Phases (12inch) - WAXRDM002
item.description: Foobar - Shifting Phases (12inch) - WAXRDM002
item.content:encoded:
We know there are copious amounts of PFAS in the water supply of Rotterdam, but there must be more! What else could explain the amount of talent this city provides?
Foobar is yet another prime example of this phenomenon. Coming of age in Burgundian Brabant and cultivated in the grimy streets of our beautiful harbour city, Foobar just has a way of looking beyond its imperfections and translating the warmer hidden sides of the city whilst still tapping into its more rugged edges in this 4 track EP, for his debut release ''Shifting Phases'' on WAXRDM.
The title track Shifting Phases just eases you into the whole, getting you ready to face another day on the grind, that's Rotterdam baby! We work hard and we play hard, and when we play, these are the sounds we wanna play too. Proper House Music.
Some serious anger management issues on Parallel Motion, hitting hard from the get go, starting off with some intimidating drums, in your face bass lines, enticing melodies & alluring vocals. All of a sudden you're 3 minutes in, and you can't even remember what got you so upset in the first place.
Who said you needed to be loud to be powerful? Not us, that's for sure, and definitely not Foobar. Quiet Strength proves that point yet again, laced with the sultry vocals by ES-V, this jam just takes you even further into your own headspace, drums that keep you in motion, melodies that keep you grounded but bass lines that let you float off into the atmosphere.
It's Monday again, another day at the office, cleaning apartments, trading cryptocurrencies or whatever the hell you do to make ends meet. Ahh damn, and now you remember what irritated you. Colleagues, employers, pay or the lack of it. It is a good thing you have Back on the grind to make it all sound relative, helping you forget and looking ahead at the weekend. The perfect come down track that moves forward.
item.dc:creator: Foobar

item.title: Onra - Nobody Has To Know (2026 repress) (LP) - ACOLPX5
item.description: Onra - Nobody Has To Know (2026 repress) (LP) - ACOLPX5
item.content:encoded:
Nobody Has To Know, first released in 2018 and now in high demand. For this one, the versatile French producer created music that reflects on the various aspects of a secret relationship pulling from R&B,New Jack Swing and Funk.
Stylistically Nobody Has To Know picks up from the Future Funk style Onra originated on his 2010's Long Distance (and its 2012 companion EP Deep In The Night for Fool's Gold). Where those two releases mined the early and mid parts of the 1980s for ideas and references, the new album digs into late '80s and early '90s jams for smoother and richer sounds. Bolstering the record are two talented multi-instrumentalists, New Zealand's Lewis McCallum and Belgium's Pomrad, who bring touches of virtuosity to Onra's trademark smooth arrangements. The result is a record that, like its theme, oscillates between tender, torrid and tumultuous.

item.title: Andrzej Dudek-Durer - Astral Meditations (LP) - HR006 BLK
item.description: Andrzej Dudek-Durer - Astral Meditations (LP) - HR006 BLK
item.content:encoded:
Forty years of cassette releases, pressed for the first time on vinyl
First of two instalments exploring the previously unreleased sonic archives of one of Poland’s most enigmatic living artists - with its first volume focused on his deep listening practice and spiritual reverie (recorded 1990–2013)
The last time Andrzej Dudek-Dürer took a banknote bearing the face of the Polish anarchist Jarosław Dąbrowski from his pocket to trade it for a pair of shoes was in 1969. He bought them for 120zł - the equivalent of 100€ today - and never replaced them since then. Only rebuilt them, year after year, drawing a needle and thread through the leather each time it split, closing one wound before the next one opened. It became a ritual of precision, stitching a record of another year into their soles.
That same year, in Wrocław, he arrived at a conclusion that would recalibrate everything that followed. Convinced he was the reincarnation of Albrecht Dürer, he adopted the surname Dudek-Dürer, stopped cutting his hair and began wearing the same garments every day. It was the first ritual of many, though he wouldn't have called it that yet. Look closely enough, over the decades, and it is always the same gesture, returning in different material: hair growing in a single unbroken strand, a needle drawing thread through leather, sitar strings pulled taut across a neck he built with his own hands and magnetic tape spooling forward inside the cassette boxes stacked against his walls.
None of this began in a vacuum. Dudek-Dürer emerged from the Wrocław neo-avant-garde, in a Polish art world where an exhibition could be cancelled overnight by the stroke of a censor's pen. In 1973, his exhibition Auto-crucifixion was shut down by the state, and for a time he found himself blocked from exhibiting his own art at all - the one force in his life that ever came close to cutting the thread.
He seemed to experience it differently. In 1974, after long, patient research into sitar craftsmanship, he built his first prototype with his brother, a knowledgeable luthier. In 1978, in a smoked-out jazz club, he took his first steps into sound recording with the unreleased album Jazz From Underground with his first band. By 1979, recognition started to travel further than he could.
Turning toward Far-Eastern philosophy, meditation and the idea of reincarnation was another language of freedom for him. It was a way of claiming an inner territory the state could not reach, a border it could not close. Mail Art served a parallel function, reaching further out: in a country that restricted travel and expression, sending and receiving art through the postal system became an act of quiet rebellion.
The body, in his understanding, is only an envelope readied for constant transformation. From this came Metaphysical Telepathy: during the years he could not leave Poland, he treated that confinement as a rehearsal room, sending his mind out ahead on the same thread his body would later follow. Living Sculpture grew from the same root with performances of stillness beside static art objects, until the boundary between the object and the man beside it simply dissolved. Camera Meditation extended the same instinct into photography: a shutter click flattening three dimensions into two so that a single instant could be held forever. Inspired by the pioneers of self-portrait photography like Robert Cornelius, he used it to document time itself, and kept explaining to me: ''You know. This is not about vanity. This is about observing time passing.”
The isolation did not end suddenly. It ended the way his own philosophy had already predicted it would, from the inside first. Mail Art quietly solved the problem politics couldn't. Correspondence built during years of confinement slowly worked its way through doors the state itself had kept locked. Contacts made through folded paper and stamps became invitations. Ultimately, invitations became passports.
In 1983 he made his first trip outside Poland, to Germany, in search of the audio technology he couldn’t get his hands on before. In 1985, he was invited by the Indian embassy in Poland to give a sitar concert on an instrument he had spent a decade patiently stringing together - half sitar, half tanpura, built from patience and determination. After the collapse of the People's Republic of Poland, the travels kept unspooling: South Korea, then Mexico, then Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Singapore, Japan and the United States - each stop leaving behind its own small knot of tape, tied off and carried home.
In the decades since, recognition arrived at the same unhurried pace: he conducted workshops at UC Berkeley, served as vice-president for artistic affairs of the Union of Polish Art Photographers and the Union of Polish Visual Artists between 2010 and 2014 and received the Bronze Medal for Merit to Culture - Gloria Artis. His visual work gradually entered collections including the National Museums of Warsaw, the Stedelijk Museum, Tate Modern, MoMA and the Venice Biennale. His musical practice, by contrast, never found that kind of room - left to circulate quietly, sharing his cassette tapes directly, waiting for someone willing to follow it further.
It took months before I could find a way to reach Andrzej Dudek-Dürer - his presence online is very close to nonexistent. Surprisingly, LinkedIn turned out to be the only door still open, a faintly absurd irony given everything else about him. I packed the strict minimum for a three-day trip and an empty notebook and made my way to Wrocław. His headquarters sits in the neighbourhood of Grabyszyn: a two-storey pre-war house that has belonged to his family for generations. The man who opened the door was long-haired, long-bearded, in his trademark leather shoes and patched jeans. We sat in his living room, in front of a computer where decades of recordings sat organised in cryptically named files, surrounded by books and objects that had arrived one layer at a time, leaving room for only two chairs in the middle. His shoes sat by the door, rebuilt so many times they had become their own quiet sculpture. Cassette tapes filled boxes against the walls, almost unlabelled, each one a spool of thread holding decades of sound that had never once been asked for, until now.
I listened for hours: meditating in front of strangers on the porch of a Seoul temple until the tourists stopped taking photos and simply waited with him; a stand-off with border guards at the US–Mexico crossing over an instrument they couldn't identify and didn't trust; a session with the Stockhausen family that he still, decades later, describes like it happened last week. All of it interrupted, occasionally, by the smell of soup boiling and fresh bread warming on the ceramic stove. After two days, it felt like being handed the end of a very long thread and asked, gently, to keep following it. I left with a USB drive holding his full discography, signed with his unmistakable signature.
Astral Meditations From A Living Statue is a length of that thread, drawn out from the boxes stacked against his walls - recordings gathered from different rooms, different countries, different decades. This first record breathes slowly: incense-thick, meditative, built for stillness. A cutting-edge séance in outer space where machines learn how to dream.
It begins with the neo-classical improvisations of Andrzej, space-delayed, recorded at Klub Muzyki i Literatury in Wrocław in 2002. 'When..So' opens the curtains with a deep-rooted meditation accompanied by slow-decaying piano figures illuminated by a candle-lit spirit gathering.
Los Angeles, 1990: a dormant villa, a grand piano, the voice of Bonnie Barnett. 'Exception' is captured in a single room, in a single afternoon - voice and keys circling each other, neither one leading, until the silence between the notes starts to feel like the instrument.
'The Meta...' and 'Tired Of...', recorded at Studio Morandi in Ponte Nossa, Italy, in 1992, settle into a sitar drone built entirely from patience - overtones stacking and beating against each other, strung by a man who never once set foot in India. 'Mastery Of...' follows, recorded the same year at Studio Suski in Łomianki, pushing that same hum further still, until pitch dissolves into a spectral reverie. 'Transcendental Sound', from 2000, closes the first record in a slow bath of celestial frequency - better heard beside the shores of the Odra river.
More than fifty years after deciding that a life could become an artwork, Andrzej Dudek-Dürer continues to inhabit that decision. His shoes keep wearing thin against the earth's crust. His hair keeps growing, one strand at a time. His cassette tapes keep spooling in the dark of their boxes.
Now the thread finds its last shape: a single unbroken groove, spiralling inward from the outer edge to the label at the centre. Never cut - the way nothing else in his life ever was. Drop the needle and it will find that groove and follow it, the same way a needle once followed leather, once followed a border it couldn't cross, once followed string into an instrument that didn't exist until he built it. This record is the other end of a thread that has been travelling for fifty years. For the length of both sides, it rests here, in your hands. This is a timeless proof that the Lord of the New Age was never lost.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej Dudek-Durer

item.title: Len Lewis - Paradise People + (12inch) - DUZN004
item.description: Len Lewis - Paradise People + (12inch) - DUZN004
item.content:encoded:
Len Lewis arrives on Amsterdam’s Dzungla, digging into the tech house veteran’s vault for a mix of archival material and previously unreleased cuts. Four tracks spanning from 2002 to 2021, showcasing his trademark dark, driving sound, with three tracks being released for the first time.
The A-side reissues the original Paradise People, the highly sought-after 2002 cut and enduring spaced out favourite. On the A2 comes the previously unreleased Paradise People (2003 Dub), a more dubbed-out version produced in 2003 but never released before.
The B-side opens with Bare Back, an eerie high-energy groover, while the B2, titled A1, takes things into wonkier, more stripped-back territory. Two contrasting cuts that work across the dance floor, from peak-time sets to the opening hours.

item.title: Wiersma - VSR 001 (12inch) - VSR001-R
item.description: Wiersma - VSR 001 (12inch) - VSR001-R
item.content:encoded:
Repress! Back by popular demand–VSR 001 is designed to take you to the outer reaches of where you need to go. Wiersma has created a world where with your eyes closed and head down, the dance-floor can transport you to the outer reaches of space and back again for another beautiful night with all your favorite people.
Vermilion Sun Records was started as a passion project in 2025 with a belief in the magic of physical media juxtaposed against the incursion of AI. The original release featured just 100 copies and utilized US-only distribution; it was sold out in less than 5 months. After being brought across the pond from Boston to Brussels by local DJ & tastemaker Rasaaq, it was subsequently shared, quickly gaining popularity on Discogs. This repress is a testament to Vermilion Sun’s core belief; that is meant to be shared and enjoyed by everyone, and there is magic in that ritual.
Wiersma is a cherished member of the electronic music scene in Boston/Cambridge, MA. A DJ, partygoer, and prolific producer, he has played many of the city’s favorite nights sharing bills with other local talent and setting the stage for international acts like Bradley Zero, Garrett David, and Cinthie. Tapping all of these channels brings forth a creativity where memories from nights in Boston and other global travel transform his unique productions. His release VSR 001 showcases this style, exploring the darker and proggier sides of the house universe while making sure to stay tethered to a reality with firm roots on the dancefloor. A1 begins with Once Around Vega where a cinematic opening draws you into groovy and spacey loops demanding you to move. Syntactic Roles churns more deeply, incorporating layered dystopian vocals, rolling basslines and light acidity that is sure to help you close your eyes and put your head down for a dance. The B side keeps the space station grooving with Transmission from L3, and closes out with Rules of Teleportation incorporating more vocals over chugging electro infused grooves.
item.dc:creator: Wiersma

item.title: Trolley Route - New Visual Order (12inch) - DKMNTL-UFO23
item.description: Trolley Route - New Visual Order (12inch) - DKMNTL-UFO23
item.content:encoded:
Revelling in adventurous, malleable synthesis and a strong melodic instinct, long-standing techno heavyweight Oscar Mulero brings his Trolley Route alias to Dekmantel. Across four rush-inducing cuts of studio exploration the Spanish veteran showcases a lighter side to his muse without sacrificing maximal dancefloor impact.
Oscar Mulero first debuted Trolley Route back in the early 00s through albums and EPs for Pure Plastic, Minuendo and others, offering a more playful strain of machine music to contrast with the steely output under his own name. Embracing dub textures and Detroit-coded synth leads, the recently-revived alias has become a haven for the looser styles that spill out of his studio. It just so happens these outliers are as crucial as any of Mulero's primary club smashers.
From the swampy chord sequence that dominates 'New Visual Order' to the meaty sub-bass and delay-soaked synth sweeps of 'Relativity Of The Vision', the whole EP is spilling over with madcap charm and a casual boss-level quality that can only come from a true legend letting their hair down.
item.dc:creator: Trolley Route

item.title: Marcel Dettmann - My Own Shadow: Album (2LP) - K7461LP
item.description: Marcel Dettmann - My Own Shadow: Album (2LP) - K7461LP
item.content:encoded:
Dettmann introduced My Own Shadow last year, a project where music, visual art, and photography converged in two EPs, Approaching (2025) and Faultline (2026) prior to the release of this full album. More than just a name, this project lets sound, image, and vision blend organically, reflecting his intuitive process of deconstruction, resonance, and emotional discovery.
My Own Shadow: Album is built with textural minimalism through rhythm, tension and release, embarking on a path through the recollections and experience of the dancefloor. This space remains the ultimate proving ground where history, instinct, and transcendence collide, guiding Dettmann through his musical interests.
For over three decades, Berlin-based DJ, producer, and curator Marcel Dettmann has remained a central force in electronic music, continuously pushing the boundaries of the craft. Deeply rooted in early influences ranging from post-punk and industrial to synth-pop, his dynamic DJ sets and expansive discography, including seminal releases on Ostgut Ton and Dekmantel, effortlessly weave together raw techno, Chicago house, electro, and avant-garde soundscapes. Far beyond club booths and releases on his own imprints, MDR and Bad Manners, Dettmann's multidisciplinary ethos has led him into artistic territories spanning gallery soundscapes, ballet compositions, and cinematic film scores. This relentless creative curiosity defines a career built at the intersection of dancefloor functionality, collaborative experimentation, and perpetual sonic evolution.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Dettmann

item.title: Various Artists - Past Forward: Silver (Mini-LP) - JSL 001
item.description: Various Artists - Past Forward: Silver (Mini-LP) - JSL 001
item.content:encoded:
Revisiting the sound and spirit of Jazzy Sport, rooted in Japan and carried forward by a new generation. Compiled by Nina Yamada, featuring Cro-Magnon and Grooveman Spot, with remixes by DJ Mitsu the Beats and Idjut Boys.
Founded in 2002, Jazzy Sport emerged at a particularly fertile moment in Japanese music. Beginning as an independent label and record shop, with its first store in Morioka and Jazzy Sport Music Shop Tokyo opening in Shibuya the following year, it became a home for artists including GAGLE, DJ Mitsu the Beats, Cro-Magnon and Grooveman Spot. Its releases moved freely between hip-hop, house, jazz, broken beat and live musicianship, helping define a distinctly Japanese strain of open-minded club culture.
But the music was only the beginning. Jazzy Sport developed into a network of record shops across Japan, alongside its label and distribution work, apparel and design, dance studios, and a Morioka record shop joined to a bouldering gym. These were not unrelated side projects. They expressed the same founding idea: that music, sport and everyday life could come together to create community.
PAST FORWARD: SILVER marks the first release on the Jazzy Sport London label, distributed by Time Capsule. Established in 2022, the London project first took shape through parties, radio shows and community collaborations connecting Japan and the UK. This compilation carries the Jazzy Sport archive and its values forward through a new generation.
At the centre is Nina Yamada, the daughter of one of Jazzy Sport’s core members. She grew up within the community that shaped the collective, and her selection is not a conventional greatest-hits survey, but an inside view of the catalogue and an intergenerational handover made audible.
The music moves naturally between hip-hop and house, electronic production and live performance. That openness has always been central to Jazzy Sport, where club music, musicianship and community are part of the same conversation rather than separate scenes.
DJ Mitsu the Beats’ remix of Cro-Magnon’s “Eclipse” brings the refined, soulful depth that makes him such an important figure in Japanese beat music. Idjut Boys’ deep, dubwise Cro-Magnon rework reflects the long exchange between Japan and the UK, while Grooveman Spot’s “Do The Dance” finds a sweet spot between acid-tinged 808 groove and warm soulfulness.
Elsewhere, Nubian Lady’s “In☆Flu☆Enza” draws on Detroit techno and Chicago house but sharpens those influences into something lean and distinctive. Physical Sound Sport’s “Magical Kalimba” captures the communal energy and openness of a live session. Bottom Fly’s “Rhyme Or Reason,” rooted in Morioka, pairs rough-edged beats with mellow samples and a quiet sense of nostalgia.
What comes through is not only the strength of the individual tracks, but the sensibility that connects them. That keeps PAST FORWARD: SILVER from feeling like a nostalgic best-of. For longtime followers, it offers rediscovery; for new listeners, a way into the breadth of Jazzy Sport; and for DJs, a selection made for the record bag, not just the archive.
item.dc:creator: Various Artists

item.title: Eerie Enterprises - Places Remember Events (LP) - DKMNTL118
item.description: Eerie Enterprises - Places Remember Events (LP) - DKMNTL118
item.content:encoded:
As Eerie Enterprise, upsammy and Piezo have funnelled their singular styles into a classic-feeling but ultra-modern album of elegant, angular electronica. With a strong melodic sensibility and a highly developed palette of playful sound design in their toolkit, the unexpected pairing grew spontaneous jams into a considered collaboration, and Places Remember Events is the end result.
Individually, Thessa Torsing and Luca Mucci have carved out strong identities within contemporary electronic music. As upsammy, Torsing has applied a delicate precision to ambient and uptempo approaches alike, building up a striking catalogue of releases including her 2020 LP for Dekmantel, Zoom. Meanwhile, Mucci has taken a wayward path through contemporary bass music and techno that matches edgy sound design with playful unpredictability. As Eerie Enterprise, both artists tap into their respective creative instincts while arriving at a unique sound with a nurturing quality they were both missing from modern dance music.
Having appreciated each other's work for some years, in July 2024 Torsing and Mucci seized an opportunity to carve out two days in the studio. There was no expectation of an end product, but the sketches conceived during those open-ended, hardware-oriented sessions felt worthy of a deeper exploration developed and finalised over the following year-and-a-half.
Places Remember Events has an unapologetically nostalgic streak, calling to mind the warm glow of melodically-charged, golden-era electronica. The twitchy rhythmic make-up of tracks like 'Decay + Collapse' and 'Folding Origin' speak to the duo's shared affinity for ravey energy, but even within faster frameworks they lean into half-time space to maintain a light-footed agility that allows the relatively busy arrangements to feel grounded and patient rather than frantic.
There's an appreciation for mystery in the emotional make-up of many of the tracks, not least in the slithering textural exploration and spatial tension of 'Capsule', but elsewhere fragile melancholia guides the melody direction of 'Superradiance' and 'Things Fall Upwards'. The final impression is crisp and modern while delivering an accessible experience that seeks to soothe rather than shock when so much contemporary club music tips towards uneasy intensity.
Finding malleable approaches to their chosen sonics and applying them to intentional song structures, Eerie Enterprise collectively land on a sound that promises a lasting reward for the repeat voyager — satisfying headphone gear in the grand tradition of introspective electronic music, but also with a physical immediacy that will manifest in the live set upsammy and Piezo have put together to perform later in the year.
item.dc:creator: Eerie Enterprises

item.title: 808 PRINCE - 808 PRINCE (LP) - Apron808
item.description: 808 PRINCE - 808 PRINCE (LP) - Apron808
item.content:encoded:
Renowned London producer, DJ, and Apron Records founder Steven Julien taps into his alter-ego with his new album, 808 PRINCE. Written and produced around iconic drum machines, 808 Prince embraces raw drum programming, analogue textures, and bass-heavy compositions.The record moves fluidly between peak-time club energy and experimental rhythm studies, exploring the shared languages of techno, house, acid house, grime, and electro. Rather than looking back, the album reimagines the influence of the 808 through Julien’s distinct production style, creating a body of work that is both timeless and forward-looking.
The album features a strong lineup of collaborators, including James Massiah, J. Caesar, Jarren, Touch Sensitive, and KIAH, expanding Julien’s sonic universe while remaining anchored in pure groove and movement. More than an album, 808 PRINCE marks a new chapter in Steven Julien’s artistic practice, bringing together decades of club music influence, hands-on studio craftsmanship, and a lifelong fascination with rhythm into a singular statement designed for dance floors worldwide.

item.title: A Guy Called Gerald - Voodoo Ray EP (12inch) - JBOX-36
item.description: A Guy Called Gerald - Voodoo Ray EP (12inch) - JBOX-36
item.content:encoded:
There are few electronic musicians as accomplished as A Guy Called Gerald From writing genre-expanding records as a member of 808 State and as a solo artist, to crafting what journalists call the greatest jungle album ever made under the moniker Black Secret Technology, AGCG has spent four decades redefining what electronic music can be. With collaborations, remixes, and tracks for the biggest names in house, techno, drum & bass, and jazz, one thread remains constant: in any decade or any genre, AGCG's music continues to be celebrated as genre-pushing excellence.
Juice Box is AGCG's label, named after his Manchester-based soundsystem. Originally established in 1992, the label went on an unofficial hiatus before the decade's end as AGCG's output demanded wider release. pairing two essential cuts from Gerald's vault that have long deserved proper vinyl treatment. On the A-side, the absolute classic ''Voodoo Ray'' finally returns to wax. On the flip, 1990's ''I Won't Give In'' resurfaces from the archive, a reminder that even Gerald's deep cuts carry the weight of lost classics. Juice Box is back, and the catalog has plenty of treasures to unearth, along with new material from one of the all-time greats.

item.title: Isaac Kniveton - Daydreaming (12inch) - MOONANDSUN
item.description: Isaac Kniveton - Daydreaming (12inch) - MOONANDSUN
item.content:encoded:
Isaac Kniveton (fka Keplrr) steps out with Daydreaming, a four track deluge of psychedelic club projections for Call Super and Parris’ can you feel the sun imprint.
Having boasted a notable reputation as Keplrr for labels like Control Freak and Midgar, Isaac Kniveton now embraces transition. On Daydreaming, his debut release under his own name, he maintains an unclassifiable sound with newer purpose; a sound that cascades in brighter colours. It’s a renewed sense of focus and subtlety that produces some of his most arresting work to date.
The ornate funk of opener Flutter angles for the wide-eyed, a cosmic stepper that pins tight drums to a weightless melodic base. Love Groove’s inebriated swing trips out further, a steady cut that binds vocals from GRACE founder Katiusha with entangled melodies. Symmetry’s wayward rhythm ups the ante with subtle rave tension, gently rising as its circular bassline swells. On closer Molecule, he locks in for an exploratory dive, offering shades of Detroit and twisted theremins.
A fascinating new era for Isaac Kniveton that finds solace in can you feel the sun’s forward-leaning club manifesto.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Kniveton

item.title: Various Artists - Borga Revolution - Ghanaian Music In The Digital Age 1983-1992 Vol. 4 (12inch) - KALITALP013
item.description: Various Artists - Borga Revolution - Ghanaian Music In The Digital Age 1983-1992 Vol. 4 (12inch) - KALITALP013
item.content:encoded:
2xLP in gatefold sleeve, with printed inner sleeves examining the stories of the artists featured on the volume
Kalita present the fourth and final instalment of their groundbreaking ‘Borga Revolution!’ series, uncovering another selection of essential recordings from the rich and far-reaching world of Ghanaian highlife. Volume 4 brings together rare recordings from artists such as Rex Omar, Nat Fredua, and CST Amankwah, alongside the elusive, deeply hypnotic and beautiful sounds of the Abibifo Dance Band of Ghana (led by the legendary bassist Ralph Karikari) and Baffour Kyei.
Spanning deep, hypnotic highlife through to the vibrant electronic productions of 1980s Burger Highlife, Volume 4 captures a period of extraordinary musical change, as Ghanaian artists absorbed influences from funk, disco, boogie, and new synthesizer technology. With previous volumes championed by tastemakers including Gilles Peterson, Antal, Tom Ravenscroft, and Hunee, this final chapter turns its attention once again to the music of the Ghanaian diaspora.
Volume 4 brings together rare recordings from artists such as Rex Omar, Nat Fredua, and CST Amankwah, alongside the elusive, deeply hypnotic and beautiful sounds of the Abibifo Dance Band of Ghana (led by the legendary bassist Ralph Karikari) and Baffour Kyei. Unearthing recordings that have languished in obscurity for over forty years, the compilation moves between deep highlife, rhythmic dancefloor cuts, and pioneering digital productions, revealing yet more musical ingenuity of Ghanaian artists both home and abroad. The final instalment in the ‘Borga Revolution!’ series, it offers another vital collection of forgotten favourites and hidden treasures for DJs, collectors, and anyone drawn to the endlessly inventive sounds of Ghanaian music.
The 1970s and 80s saw Ghanaian musicians begin to incorporate Western sounds like funk and disco into their music, reflecting thechanging global musical landscape. However, the country's political instability and economic hardships, marked by military regimes and curfews, forced many artists to leave Ghana in search of better opportunities abroad. In Europe and the U.S., these musicians fused their traditional highlife roots with emerging digital sounds, using cutting-edge technology like the DX7 synthesizer and drum machines to create the genre now known as Burger Highlife.
With ‘Borga Revolution!’ Kalita offers a vivid exposition of this musical transformation, using rare interviews, archival photos, and detailed liner notes to bring to life the pioneering spirit of both well-known icons and unsung innovators of Ghanaian Highlife, one of West Africa’s most exciting musical movements.
item.dc:creator: Various Artists

item.title: Discoteca Tropicana - Discoteca Tropicana (12inch) - SLVDSCS11
item.description: Discoteca Tropicana - Discoteca Tropicana (12inch) - SLVDSCS11
item.content:encoded:
Selva Discos is proud to present its latest release: the EP by the band Discoteca Tropicana. This record features 4 original tracks that celebrate the rhythms that have influenced Brazilian disco music, showcasing the best of this fusion: the swing and tropical flavour that bring sunshine to any dance floor.
The project is the result of a collaboration between Kiko Costato, the enfant terrible of the Brazilian music scene, and Ze Nigro, a producer and multi-instrumentalist who has won two Grammy Awards and has worked with major names in Brazilian and international music such as Joao Donato, Antonio Carlos & Jocafi and Natasha Diggs.
This EP is based on 4 different themes. For each one, Kiko and Ze Nigro recruited some of Brazil’s finest studio musicians – people who work with Seu Jorge, Ceu, Criolo, Metá Metá, Cidadao Instigado and Tulipa Ruiz – as well as pioneering artists from the Brazilian Black music scene, such as the backing vocalists who work with the legendary Gilberto Gil.
Corpos Celestes is a more classic disco diva track, featuring string arrangements and a grand piano, as if it were the start of the evening, a magical moment straight from the heyday of disco in the United States; Corpo Treme is the sweat, the vuco-vuco, a song for that moment when you’ve already let yourself go, a sprint to the frenetic rhythm of the carimbó; Tobina is the meeting of Brazil and Africa, from which Brazilian swing is born, an original chant straight from the Congo, with a characteristic African guitar, adapted to Brazilian rhythms, just like the afoxe. Finally, the dancefloor hit Nao Pode Acabar, a more urban disco track, which works just as well for kicking off a party with the right vibe as for closing a set with the highest energy.

item.description: Roman Khropko - Among The Machines EP (12inch) - OBI03
item.content:encoded: Roman Khropko delivers four cuts balancing precision club mechanics with flashes of emotion. The record moves between stripped minimal techno and warmer electro, designed to unfold gradually. The A side opens with Glimpse, a straight-forward roller driven by tight drums and a suspenseful build. Piece of Truth follows with a funkier swing, blending elastic basslines with subtle tech house inflections that keep things in motion. On the B side, Fractum settles into a hypnotic minimal tech mood, laying steady groundwork for an extended club stretch. The closing track, Among The Machines, shifts into emotional electro territory, carrying melodic tension that leaves a melancholic aftertaste. A concise and functional toolset for the dancefloor. This is one to stay in your bag for a long time.

item.title: Stone Music - Into The Cosmic Forest (LP) - ZORN120
item.description: Stone Music - Into The Cosmic Forest (LP) - ZORN120
item.content:encoded: Stone Music returns with Into the Cosmic Forest, a deep and patient journey into open-air improvisation. The group was founded in 2022 by Tokio Hasegawa, a core member of the legendary Taj Mahal Travellers, and brings together a wide circle of musicians from Japan’s ambient and experimental scenes. While the name is new, the spirit continues. Stone Music extends the free-form, site-responsive approach that defined Taj Mahal Travellers — music shaped by environment, duration, and collective awareness rather than fixed structure. Into the Cosmic Forest consists of two long-form pieces, each exceeding 20 minutes, both recorded live outdoors. Side A was captured at Japan’s Off-Tone Festival. It unfolds slowly and organically - layers of voice, strings, electronics, wind instruments, and percussive textures gradually forming a shifting sonic landscape. Side B was recorded on the grounds of Mithila Museum in the mountains of Niigata, an art space managed by Hasegawa himself. More intimate in atmosphere yet equally immersive, the piece centers on voice and subtle interplay, allowing space and silence to become part of the composition. What you hear is direct and unpolished: air moving, sound resonating, musicians responding to each other and to their surroundings in real time. Following tours in India during 2023-24, with performances in national museums and universities, Stone Music continues to explore music as shared space rather than spectacle. Into the Cosmic Forest invites listeners into that space - unedited, unhurried, and fully alive.
item.dc:creator: Stone Music

item.title: Adiciatz - Musique Domestique (LP) - ZORN117
item.description: Adiciatz - Musique Domestique (LP) - ZORN117
item.content:encoded: Musique Domestique marks the debut full-length from French duo Adiciatz, a project that emerges from the shared musical curiosity of Manon Nogier and Guillaume Lespinasse. Living near Lyon and making music together since before the pandemic, the pair developed their sound during lockdown improvisations at home - a creative process that quickly revealed a unique musical chemistry rooted as much in folk tradition as in experimental exploration. Drawing on a wide palette of influences - from Occitan poetry, delicate folk to drone and spontaneous sound exploration - Adiciatz makes music that feels both intimate and expansive. Nogier’s voice and amplified taisho koto weave through Lespinasse’s keyboards, machines and percussive touches, forming a sonic world where ritualistic soft folk melodies coexist with subtle electronic textures. Their live performances, including an appearance at the Meakusma Festival, where their set blurred the line between concert and seance, have already shown how this blend comes to life in front of audiences, with hypnotic vocals, spiralling chords and slow, trance-like rhythms inviting listeners into a space that is both meditative and evocative. On Musique Domestique, those live-rooted sensibilities are distilled into recorded form. The album moves fluidly between rich pastoral folk and instrumental meanderings. Musique Domestique announces Adiciatz as a compelling new voice at the intersection of folk, experimental and electronic music crafted with care and intuition.
item.dc:creator: Adiciatz

item.title: Jakob Bro & Midori Takada - From Such A Blue Sky (LP) - LLM038
item.description: Jakob Bro & Midori Takada - From Such A Blue Sky (LP) - LLM038
item.content:encoded: What feels like a dream, a portal between worlds, a shimmering of ideas – that liminal space is the departure point for Midori Takada and Jakob Bro’s ever-unfolding musical friendship. On their second outing From Such A Blue Sky, arriving on Copenhagens Loveland Music in October, the compositions are transformative, and the sounds travel between immediate emotional and abstract planes. The classically trained Japanese percussionist Midori Takada, later dubbed an ambient pioneer for the landmark 1983 album Through The Looking-Glass (another portal), left behind her Western classical training and found her own paths, drawing on African and Indonesian drumming, minimalism, theater, environmental music and instant composing. Similarly, Danish composer and guitarist Jakob Bro creates otherworldly sounds and beautiful, delicate melodies through intuitive creation and collective listening. On From Such A Blue Sky the music is co-composed and created in the studio over three days, from early morning to sundown. The compositions are increasingly open ecosystems, and the range of sound sources expands significantly from the puristic Until I Met You, with Thai gongs, heavy drums, ceramic flutes, electric guitar and pedals adding to the sonic imagery of From Such A Blue Sky. From Such A Blue Sky is the second album in a trilogy recorded at AVACO Studios in Tokyo, a studio in Shinjuku renowned for its sound works in Japanese film since 1952. The trilogy is an ongoing continuation of their musical friendship, which has already led them to duo performances at World Expo Osaka, Tessenkai Noh Theatre Tokyo, Pierre Boulez Saal Berlin and Roskilde Festival.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Bro & Midori Takada

item.content:encoded: AMEN is a word that moves between the sacred and the ordinary, across languages and cultures. An ancient, universal expression, born in prayer yet living beyond it in daily life, especially in the Italian language, where it has become part of ordinary speech, used to accept, conclude, affirm, and let things be. item.title: Archimboldos - Crusta Arcana (LP) - ZORN121
item.description: Archimboldos - Crusta Arcana (LP) - ZORN121
item.content:encoded: Archimboldos have clawed their way out of the starcaves of their primordial past and into the tranquil light of a coral garden on their third full length album, Crusta Arcana, a gumbo stewpot of transcendent electronica suffused with tribal rhythms and liquid ambience. Across a stereo field smeared with tolling bells, post-industrial folk percussion, and tinkling keys, Archimboldos soundtrack a science fictional journey, not into the depths of space, but deep beneath the waves. In the past the Chilean duo of Nicolás Carcavilla and Felipe Crocco have described their music as “liminal shrimp folk.” Here they continue this strange exploration when they visit the court of the prawns, producing stately electronic chamber orchestrations. Perhaps these are the frequencies used for ritual dream initiation into the mystery schools of drowned Atlantis. Weaving an ancient sacred science, Archimboldos take listeners on a mystic vovage into their singular crustacean mythology, the crusta of their hidden arcana. Archimbolodos are masters of conjoining cyclonic and centrifugal lines of electricity into spellbinding incantations. These deep-sea transmissions envelope the listener into aquamarine forcefields that are as hallucinatory as they are hypnotic. Navigating these strange fantasias could lead one to getting lost at sea, but the work is buoyed by the somnolent melodies of lonely harpsichords and swelling synth pads whose sustained tones reach towards distant shores. Sailing across a vast expanse of oceanic harmonies and percolating percussion, these pieces are as precise as the hand of a sailor on the rudder, moving with the tide. Casting their net wide across eight pieces, Archimboldos have made a big catch. From the emotive electronic counterpoint found on Bursting Armor to the blocks of seaweed tangled sonic sculpture trawled up from the ocean floor on Aphelion IX. Other songs are like samples of biological ambience collected from luminous tide pools: resplendent tones placed into a Petri dish of sound, swirled, cultured and fermented until it undulates with the rhythmic movement of microscopic lifeforms. Alternating between rippling minimalist sonority and pounding, progressive, synth-heavy entrancement, Crusta Arcana charts its own idiosyncratic itinerary of instrumental invention. All the while light is down streaming from the heavens to pierce the waters, here calm, there choppy. The intrepid musical captains commanding Archimboldos have laid a course for new archipelagos of the imagination, guided by heavenly constellations.
item.dc:creator: Archimboldos

item.title: Cop Tears - The Rules Of The Game (LP) - TTT114
item.description: Cop Tears - The Rules Of The Game (LP) - TTT114
item.content:encoded: Pure loveliness. Proper music-making, DIY Classical, but nothing slapdash or posey. Intimate and tentative, seamed with risk, occasional mis-steps, dodgy tuning, minor technical fuck-ups; but driven by gripping, stilled dedication and deep musical understanding. Double bass, electric guitar, flute, melodica, singing; recorded at home in NYC, on dodgy gear, with snug, woody, shhshh-ing, analogue-style ambience. The trio hovers between cheerful relish - who’s that giggling at the back - and hushed, humble reverence, basking in the processes of musical communion and learning. They play like they are gingerly passing on a precious, fragile gift; but without prissy conceit. Luminous selections from the last six hundred years - John of Dunstable meets Friedrich Nietzsche - are lovingly arranged by the group, with a bent for stripped-to-the-bone, emotionally restrained sublimity, steady as she blows. Very warmly recommended. Soul food.
item.dc:creator: Cop Tears

item.title: Jakob Bro - 8 (LP) - LLM033
item.description: Jakob Bro - 8 (LP) - LLM033
item.content:encoded:
Jakob Bro, Brian Blade, Craig Taborn, Chris Cheek, Jesper Zeuthen, Anders Christensen, Larry Grenadier & Marcus Gilmore, playing compositions by Paul Motian and Jakob Bro. The album was recorded in a single session at New York’s Power Station with engineer James Farber, following a week-long residency at the Village Vanguard.
‘Danish guitarist and composer Jakob Bro is celebrated for his pure reflective expression and penchant for celestial textures, effortlessly distilling and refining quiet sonics. At the Village Vanguard, he leads an impressive group – featuring two bassists and two drummers – for a nearly week-long residency. ‘The perfectly poised, ambient-leaning soundworld that characterizes Bro’s compositions was discomposed and distended by this octet, probing thrilling sounds and providing ample opportunity to create spontaneously. It was an exhilarating jazz night with some of the most esteemed players out there.’ (Jazztrail)

item.title: Thomas Bush - Random Constraint Satisfaction Problems (LP) - ZORN118
item.description: Thomas Bush - Random Constraint Satisfaction Problems (LP) - ZORN118
item.content:encoded:
A new album of category-scrambling song-craft by the elusive and shape-shifting Thomas Bush; the latest stage in a wayward path between everything from murky dirges to head-nodding laments to crystalline synths that hang precariously in the air over your new-favourite bass line. Critical responses along the way have focussed on a predilection for the folkey-dokey, but judging from releases like 2026s guld, Bushs definition of folk has as much to do with A Guy Called Gerald as it does with Shirley Collins or John Martyn. For all its diversity, what unites Bushs ever-expanding body of work is its dual commitment to experimentation and a job well done.
Random Constraint Satisfaction Problems was recorded at Vista Studio 1, Malmö, between 2022 and 2025. After creating an account at academia.edu for the purpose of reading a text now forgotten, I began to get emails asking me questions such as Thomas Bush, did you write Brucellosis and Sacroiliitis: A Common Presentation of an Uncommon Pathogen?, and Are you the Thomas Bush who wrote ATR-dependent Phosphorylation of FANCA on Serine 1449 after DNA Damage is Important for FA Pathway Function?, which began to make me wonder if I was, or if I wasnt, perhaps I should be. The resulting work is an attempt to find meaning in this, and other chaotic and ambiguous situations through analysis using materials and equipment to hand. Being sensitive to signs and following them up with enthusiasm. Both source material and evaluation are presented.

item.title: Matas Petrikas - The Unknown (Deadbeat remix) (Mini-LP) - DNG-003
item.description: Matas Petrikas - The Unknown (Deadbeat remix) (Mini-LP) - DNG-003
item.content:encoded:
Meet Matas Petrikas, a music producer, DJ, and book author with a passion for electronic music. Born in Lithuania during the time when it was still a part of the Soviet Union, Matas began experimenting with electronic sounds during his teenage years using self-built instruments and recording equipment. In 1991, Matas took a trip to Berlin that would change his life forever. There, he encountered the early years of techno culture, which led him to co-found EXEM, one of the first house and techno bands in the former Soviet space. With EXEM, Matas was one of the pioneers of electronic dance music in Lithuania, and by the end of the decade, they had charted numerous hits. They performed live shows ranging from intimate clubs to massive arenas, sewing the seeds of the local electronic music scene. Since then he relocated to Berlin and has forged a musical solo career focused on live-sets, experimentation, and authoring the book The Joy of Electronic Music.
The Unknown is Matas first release on his newly formed imprint Dang? Records, focused on supporting electronic music from Lithuania and the Baltics. The 6 track EP forges his love for texture heavy hypnotic techno with industrial and warehouse leaning low end and percussion. Although mainly an EP rooted in driving a groove, the use of earworm worthy basslines, rave breaky drums, and squelchy lead synths is where Matas long career foray into many genres of electronic music shines through.
Dang? Records releases electronic music from Lithuania and the Baltics-sounds that emerge from underwater, carried by artists who inherited the weight of transformation.

item.description: Makz - TSR004 (12inch) - TSR004
item.content:encoded: After years of shaping his sound, Makz steps forward with his debut EP. No big statements, just four tracks that speak for themselves. On the A side, Clubmate sets things in motion with a steady drive. Execution Style follows up with heavy drums and a rolling bassline that keeps pushing forward. On the flip, Ferro brings his own take on Clubmate. His DDC Tornado remix pulls the track into a deeper, more hypnotic space, made for those later hours. B2, 926813, is a small nod to The Set Crew. Light in name, but the track itself carries real weight. No gimmicks, no extras. Just honest house music, built for the floor.
